top.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, world’s top court rules
top.summary: Judgment ends seven-year legal battle and is seen as critical test for dealing with most serious of all state crimes Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority in its 2016-17 military campaign, the world’s highest court has ruled. The judgment from the international court of justice (ICJ) – which has never previously found a state responsible for genocide – ends a seven-year legal battle and is seen as a critical global test for dealing with the most serious of all state crimes.

articles.title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
articles.summary: In August 2017, after attacks by a Rohingya militia, Myanmar’s army launched a “clearance campaign” in Rakhine state, with survivors describing mass killings, rapes and burned villages as hundreds of thousands fled to Bangladesh. The Gambia took Myanmar to the ICJ in 2019, and after a seven-year legal fight the court has ruled that Myanmar committed acts of genocide. Meanwhile some 1.2 million Rohingya remain in crowded camps, unable to return home.

articles.title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
articles.summary: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during the 2017 military operations in the northern Rakhine State.
